newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain state deficit's trend favorable - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Spain state deficit's trend favorable - Salomon.

text.p: Spain's February state deficit was more stable in the two first months of the year making the trend outlook favourable for the year, Salomon Brother London wrote in a note to its clients on Wednesday.
The January-February State deficit on a national account basis amounted to 286.5 billion pesetas, almost unchanged from the 286.8 billion pesetas from the year ago period.
In January, the Spanish state deficit rose by 40.3 percent to 399.5 billion pesetas, due to seasonal and extraordinary effects.

The state deficit target for the year is 2.5 percent of gross domestic product, with three percent set for the full public sector. Last year ended with a ratio at 4.4 percent for public sector and at 3.3 percent for the state.

"The January-February outturn appears compatible with the annual target, because tax revenues are growing faster than budgeted, while the rapid rise in transfers and in interest payments likely will be redressed in coming months," Salomon Brother in London wrote.

The note added that interest payments, which rose 36.3 percent at the end of February, are expected to stabilise at 1996 level and the favourable calendar effects on transfers should get diluted in coming months.

Salomon added that the use of cash balances, falling by 557 billion pesetas to 1.97 trillion at the end of February, allowed a decline in the state gross debt of 607 billion pesetas despite rising financing needs.

"By failing to roll over all expiring bills and bonds, the Treasury started to use massive privatisations and accumulated cash balances to engineer a significant reduction in the debt-to-GDP ratio this year to raise changes of early participation in EMU," Salomon's said.
